definitions.explanation: A type of small, mild-flavored mushroom commonly used in Japanese cooking. The commercially grown variety (ぶなしめじ) grows in clusters with small round caps on slender stems.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}にしめじを{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put shimeji mushrooms in the miso soup.

examples.japanese: しめじは{一年中|いちねんじゅう}スーパーで{手|て}に{入|はい}るので{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: Shimeji mushrooms are convenient because they're available at the supermarket year-round.

notes:
One of the most common mushrooms in Japanese home cooking. The commercially cultivated variety sold in supermarkets is technically ぶなしめじ (beech shimeji), which grows in clusters. It has a mild, slightly nutty flavor and a firm texture that holds up well in cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- しめじの{炒|いた}め{物|もの}: stir-fried shimeji
- しめじの{味噌汁|みそしる}: miso soup with shimeji
- しめじの{炊|た}き{込|こ}みご{飯|はん}: shimeji mixed rice

RELATED WORDS:
- えのき: enoki mushroom — another very common supermarket mushroom
- しいたけ: shiitake mushroom — the most well-known Japanese mushroom internationally
- まいたけ: maitake mushroom — another popular cooking mushroom
- きのこ: mushroom — the general term
